main_damage_causes: The film corpus is extremely limited — only two Knight Bus scenes from Prisoner of Azkaban are present, featuring only Ernie Prang (the bus driver), not Ernie Macmillan (the Hufflepuff student), who is the subject of the bulk of the book corpus

All of Ernie Macmillan's characterization — his pomposity, his accusation of Harry as Slytherin's heir, his apology, his DA membership, his prefect anxiety, his Battle of Hogwarts Patronus — appears extensively in the book corpus but has no corresponding film corpus material to compare against

Without film corpus scenes featuring Ernie Macmillan, the scoring system's anti-hallucination rules prevent assigning damage scores to his many absent or altered book moments, severely limiting the damage assessment despite a low FP score of 33

damaging_scenes.scene: Film corpus scenes 1-2 (Knight Bus scenes, POA): Ernie Prang is a background driver with no characterization beyond physical description and minimal grunts
damaging_scenes.book_baseline: Book corpus scenes 48-61: Ernie Prang is a distinct character with a name, personality traits (collywobbles about Azkaban guards, shivering at mention of them), dialogue exchanges with Stan, and an 'owlish face' that peers interestedly at Harry
damaging_scenes.film_portrayal: Ernie Prang is entirely silent and undifferentiated in the film corpus — all dialogue and personality that belongs to him in the books (collywobbles line, shivering, conversational back-and-forth with Stan) is either cut or reassigned. The film corpus shows him only as a visual presence described as 'unshaven wizard in thick glasses' with no spoken lines attributed to him.
damaging_scenes.explanation: Ernie Prang is a minor character and his absence from meaningful dialogue causes only local damage. His few book moments establish a warm, nervous personality that contrasts with Stan's bravado, but this is a small supporting role and its loss does not affect any major arc or relationship.
